Issued at 317 PM CDT Fri Sep 25 2026

At the synoptic scale, broad ridging remains in place at the upper-
levels across much of the central CONUS. To the east, a closed upper-
level trough has remained mostly stationary over the East Coast, 
while another upper-level trough over the PNW flanks the ridge. With 
the ridge in place over the central CONUS, flow has effectively 
remained blocked over the forecast area, keeping us within a 
relative stagnant pattern for the past few days. However, continued 
impulses within the low-level flow have served to displace us within 
the periphery of the ridge. This has opened us to on-and-off 
precipitation chances with enhanced synoptic ascent from greater 
influence with passing shortwaves, as well as sustained warm/moist 
advection from the south/southwest. This blocking will allow our 
forcing and rain chances to linger until at least Sunday afternoon.

Shower activity has remained nebulous throughout the day today, 
driven primarily by weak synoptic ascent from embedded shortwaves in 
the atmospheric flow alongside sustained WAA in the low-levels. This 
activity is expected to continue through the remainder of the day 
today while warm/moist advection persists. Activity has 
remained mostly isolated/scattered and subsevere in nature; this
is expected to continue being the trend with minimal 
instability and poor effective shear for any organized 
convection. The presence of marginal MUCAPE (~100-200 J/kg) 
suggests there is low-end potential for some rumbles of thunder 
through the remainder of the afternoon. However, these 
probabilities remain on the lower end (~10-15%). Greater 
intrusion of dry air in the low-levels looks to decrease 
precipitation chances through this evening, before returning 
overnight as shortwave and associated intensifying LLJ traverse 
to the west/northwest of the forecast area. The greatest 
potential for precipitation overnight resides across 
northwestern MO and far northeastern KS (70-90%), with 
isolated/scattered showers further towards central MO. Similar 
to today, severe chances remain on the lower end with poor 
environmental parameters for any robust activity.

As the shortwave retreats towards the north/northeast with a 
diminishing LLJ, precipitation chances will lower across the 
forecast area through Saturday. Surface high pressure will gradually 
slide off towards the north and east as the upper-level ridge axis 
is displaced by the upper-level trough lifting across the northern 
CONUS. This will shift precipitation chances back over the forecast 
area by late Saturday evening with the passage of another impulse in 
the atmospheric flow. Severe chances continue to remain low with 
meager instability and shear effectively capped off during this 
timeframe, but lightning remains a risk with these storms (15-30%) 
with marginally better MUCAPE than previous days.

While the upper-level trough continues to lift off towards the 
north, and the closed low over the East Coast persists, ridging will 
build back over the central CONUS and serve to dry conditions out 
through the remainder of the weekend into early next week. The 
northward and eastward progression of the ridge (and ultimate 
evolution of the blocking pattern) will determine temperature trends 
for Monday onward, with appreciable spread in the 25th-75th 
percentile temperatures noted in probabilistic guidance. The 
influence of an energetic trough over the West Coast will help to 
break down the ridge going into midweek, and keep the remainder of 
the forecast wetter as the jet interacts with a remnant tropical 
system near southern California. This interaction with the remnant 
tropical system will further enhance atmospheric moisture content, 
leading to impressive PWAT values for this time of year. With these 
anomalously high PWAT values, trends will need to be monitored for 
the threat of flooding into next week. Temperatures will remain 
seasonable through the duration of the forecast period, with high 
temperatures in the 70s and low 80s during much of the period.
